analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md (documentation), and the supplied evidence is the base text plus a truncated patch excerpt. The visible changes add a note on shutdown unload behavior (waits up to 15 s per model; a model whose native retirement never finishes is left to process exit) and extend the `darkbloom status` documentation with a restart-needed configuration change line, which uses daemon-state fields `enabled_models_at_start` and `enabled_models_at_last_switch`, and with retry-on-memory-free text. These alter no code or controls. I found no regression against the threat model. Checked against the model: T-041/prefix cache, T-010/T-029 availability, A-018/TB-012 hold lines, TB-011 traffic eligibility and T-053 logout language. The docs make no new security-relevant claims about attestation, authorization, encryption or custody. The base text's logout statement that only HTTP 204 confirms remote revocation is unchanged. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the status bullet rewrite was not visible. The shutdown note refers to ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown, which is not in the supplied evidence. Skipping a stuck unload until process exit could mean residual GPU/KV memory (T-028) is released only on exit. This is a code-behavior question the docs cannot establish, so it is not a finding. A later pass should confirm that the code behind these docs matches them, particularly the shutdown unload timeout and the new status fields. The new daemon-state fields expose only enabled model IDs, which are already public via heartbeats.
